kicker: Continuous batching on a DGX Spark

scenes.headline: How one small box serves dozens of chat users
scenes.sub: vLLM's continuous batching on a DGX Spark
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Driftwood! A DGX Spark is a desk-sized box. Yet with vLLM it chats with dozens of people at once, on a thirty-five-billion-parameter model. Here's how.

scenes.text: Decoding one token streams every weight through the chip. So stack every live user's next token into one pass, and share that load.
scenes.say: The trick: decoding one token means streaming all the weights through the chip. So stack every live user's next token into one pass, and share that cost.

scenes.title: One user, or everyone at once

left.title: One stream per pass
items: Stream all the weights from memory
left.say: Decoding for one user streams all the weights through the chip, to multiply a single token. The compute units sit idle, waiting on memory.

right.title: Every live stream per pass
items: One fused matmul over every stream's token
right.say: Stack every user's current token and run one fused multiply against the weights already fetched. The expensive load is shared.

steps.label: Static: each group waits for its slowest
steps.say: Static batching would run a group of requests until the longest one finishes. One long answer stalls everyone.

steps.label: Continuous: join and leave at any step
steps.say: vLLM rebuilds the batch at every decode step. A new request joins on the next step; a finished one leaves and frees its memory at once.

items.say: Each user's KV cache is stored as fixed-size blocks, like virtual memory pages.

items.text: Blocks come from one shared pool
items.say: Blocks come on demand from one shared pool, so sixty-four caches of different lengths pack tightly.

items.text: Memory, not FLOPs, sets the limit
items.say: So KV-cache memory, not compute, is what caps how many users fit.

scenes.title: Aggregate tokens per second, Qwen3.6-35B, NVFP4
scenes.note: per user it falls from 85 to 22 tok/s
scenes.say: On this four-bit mixture of experts, aggregate throughput roughly triples from one user to sixteen, while each user's own stream falls from eighty-five to twenty-two tokens a second.

scenes.text: Decode is memory-bound, so share each weight load across every live stream. That buys capacity, not any one user's speed.
scenes.mark: share each weight load across every live stream

recap: Decode streams every weight for one token
Batch every live stream, rebuilt each step
KV-cache memory caps how many fit
scenes.say: To recap: memory-bound decode, one shared pass per step, and KV-cache memory deciding how many users fit.
